findings.line: repo.py:121-144 (no timeout on proc.communicate, L144); git_service.py:207-218 (_auth_env sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 at 217 but not GIT_ASKPASS), 230-260 (wait_for 300s at 251; kill parent only at 253; second await communicate at 254)
findings.finding: A wrong/expired credential does not fail fast: on a 401, git consults GIT_ASKPASS before giving up. The app never neutralizes GIT_ASKPASS (only GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0), and neither clone path can recover from a prompting askpass helper: (1) _clone_and_activate awaits proc.communicate() with no timeout at all - the background task is pinned forever and the Repo row stays status='cloning' with no error; (2) _run_git's asyncio.wait_for timeout kills only the direct git child, then awaits a second proc.communicate() which cannot return while surviving grandchildren (git-remote-http, askpass) hold the stdout/stderr pipe write ends (orphaned-pipe cancel gap) - the baseline suite shows the test exceeding a 600s pytest-timeout although its only bounded inner call is the 300s path.
findings.evidence: Live reproduction 2026-10-02: pytest tests/test_b1_clone_security.py::test_wrong_token_fails_and_is_not_echoed hangs reproducibly in isolation (45s pytest-timeout fired twice). Hang process tree: git clone -- http://127.0.0.1:44529/repo.git (pid 67023) -> git remote-http / git-remote-http (67024/67025) -> /bin/sh /usr/share/qoder-ide/resources/app/extensions/git/dist/askpass.sh "Password for 'http://127.0.0.1:44529'" (67063) -> qoder-ide askpass-main.js (67066). /proc/67023/environ shows GIT_ASKPASS=/usr/share/qoder-ide/resources/app/extensions/git/dist/askpass.sh and VSCODE_GIT_ASKPASS_NODE/MAIN alongside the app's own GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Baseline suite: both clone tests hit the 600s pytest-timeout (/tmp/qoder_full_suite.log lines 14763-14872, FAILED list lines 15569-15570 of /tmp/qoder_failures.txt); for test_background_clone_and_pull_use_env_credentials_not_url (test file line 511) the captured log (suite log lines 14874-14878) shows two successful authenticated clones ('Repo cloned and activated' twice) followed by the hang in step 3, the wrong-token clone, with no 'Clone failed' line ever emitted (repo.py:156 unreached).
findings.production_impact: In any deployment whose service environment exports GIT_ASKPASS or a GUI credential helper (desktop/IDE-hosted dev instances; interactive terminals), a user entering a wrong/expired PAT pins the clone background task indefinitely and leaves the repo permanently status='cloning' with no error, timeout, or retry. In a clean server environment (no askpass/TTY) git fails fast, which is why CI cannot catch it. Independently of environment, defect (1) makes every credential-failure clone unbounded by design.
findings.confidence: High (live repro + process-level environment evidence + code-level cancel-gap analysis)
findings.recommendation: Set GIT_ASKPASS=/bin/true, SSH_ASKPASS=/bin/true and disable credential helpers (extend GIT_CONFIG_* or -c credential.helper=) in _auth_env and repo.py:111-115 alongside GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0; wrap _clone_and_activate's communicate() in asyncio.wait_for with start_new_session=True and os.killpg on timeout; apply the same process-group kill to _run_git's timeout path (git_service.py:252-255); on timeout set Repo.status='error' with a 'clone timed out' message.

findings.location: v2 gating functions vs production call sites; epics.py policy-approval endpoint
findings.line: engine_v2.py:1-5 (docstring claim), 59-82, 85-109, 112-131 (check_file_against_policies / check_files_against_policies / has_approval - zero production callers); api/epics.py:348-374 (record_approval only wired function, called at 356)
findings.finding: Policy Engine v2 is documented as 'Adds approval rules on top of the v1 hard-coded denylist... adding a rule = DB insert', but its entire enforcement half has no production call site: check_file_against_policies / check_files_against_policies / has_approval are referenced only by backend/tests/pending/test_manager_integration.py:128 (repo-wide grep; tests/test_policy_v2.py:7 exercises only match_pattern_sync). The only wired function is record_approval, reached via POST /{epic_id}/policy-approval (approver-gated). Nothing ever reads a recorded approval or blocks on a blocking=True policy match, so DB policies gate nothing. Additionally the unwired matchers compare raw file_path strings without normalization (engine_v2.py:72/97; no realpath/normpath), so ./secrets/x, secrets/../secrets/x or absolute paths would dodge any *secrets* rule if wired as-is.
findings.evidence: Grep for engine_v2 across backend: exactly 3 files (api/epics.py:356, tests/pending/test_manager_integration.py:128, tests/test_policy_v2.py:7). No write chokepoint (base_graph._policy_check, base_graph.py:1042-1102) or handler guard consults the policies/policy_approvals tables. _glob_to_regex (engine_v2.py:18-38) then regex.match(file_path) at 72 with no path normalization.
findings.production_impact: A misleading control: operators inserting a blocking policy row (or relying on the documented second approval layer) get no enforcement - only an approval audit trail. No active bypass of the v1 floor exists; the gap is between a documented capability and its real wiring.
findings.confidence: High (absence of callers verified by exhaustive grep)
findings.recommendation: Either wire check_files_against_policies + has_approval into _policy_check before the v1 floor (with realpath-normalized paths and 'no approval => deny' for blocking rules), or explicitly mark v2 gating as dormant-not-enforced in the module docstring and endpoint description. Cross-flagged to audits 11 (dead code) and 12 (feature wiring).

findings.location: QA/devops scoped bash allowlist - absolute-path reads not confined to worktree in host-fallback mode
findings.line: tools.py:1513-1529 (_QA_ALLOWED_PREFIXES incl. 'cat ' at 1524 and 'head ' at 1525), 1795-1813 (QA bash: allowlist-only check at 1797), 1838-1856 (devops bash; allowlist from settings.devops_bash_allowlist, config.py:430); bash.py:178-194 (sandbox branch) vs 196-213 (host branch, shell=True, no containment)
findings.finding: The QA bash allowlist admits 'cat ' and 'head ' prefixes and validates only through check_allowlisted_command (which correctly rejects chaining metacharacters). Arguments are never confined to the worktree. With the default BASH_SANDBOX_ENABLED=true the command runs in the sandbox container (only cwd mounted), so cat /etc/passwd reads the container's own file - contained. With the explicit operator opt-out BASH_SANDBOX_ENABLED=false, _run_bash_command_raw executes on the host via subprocess.run(shell=True), so cat /etc/passwd, cat ~/.ssh/config or any service-user-readable absolute path is returned into the model context and LLM providers.
findings.evidence: tools.py:1797 (check_allowlisted_command only), bash.py:178-194 vs 196-213; config.py:1178-1181 (bash_sandbox_enabled default True - the gap is opt-out-mode only).
findings.production_impact: Confined to deployments that explicitly disable the sandbox (a documented escape hatch for hosts that cannot run Docker). Read-only exposure of host files readable by the service user to the model context; not a write or execution escalation.
findings.recommendation: For read-only prefixes ('cat ', 'head '), reject absolute paths and '..' segments (or resolve and require worktree containment) independent of sandbox mode; keep the existing metachar rejection.

findings.line: ci.yml:17-18 and 60-63 (Python 3.11) vs local backend/.venv (3.12); ci.yml:346 (pip-audit -r requirements.txt only); ci.yml:68/187 (requirements-dev.txt installed but never audited); ci.yml:328-346 (|| true removal per SEC-05-019 verified in place; GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-5 ignore documented at 337-345)
findings.finding: (a) CI typechecks/tests on Python 3.11 while the deployed audited venv is 3.12 - version-specific behavior untested in CI; (b) the blocking pip-audit gate covers requirements.txt only; requirements-dev.txt (pytest/mypy/ruff/black/plugins toolchain) is never audited; (c) pip-audit is not installed in the local venv (baseline failures '[Errno 2] No such file or directory: pip-audit'), so the CVE status of current pins could not be re-verified locally during this audit - per the brief, no CVE numbers are asserted; (d) one standing --ignore-vuln (GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-5) exists with an in-file justification - acceptable documented-exception pattern, but should be re-reviewed per release.
findings.evidence: ci.yml:17-18/60-63; local pytest tracebacks under python3.12; ci.yml:346 command line; requirements.txt 46 lines fully ==-pinned; requirements-dev.txt referenced for install (ci.yml:68/187) but absent from the audit step; /tmp/qoder_failures.txt pip-audit [Errno 2] entries.
findings.production_impact: Hygiene/informational: dev toolchain vulnerabilities would not gate CI; interpreter drift can mask version-specific dependency behavior. Python-jose/ecdsa migration to PyJWT verified done (ci.yml:337-345, requirements.txt:33).
findings.recommendation: Extend the pip-audit job to -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt; align CI to 3.12 (or document 3.11 as the supported floor); install pip-audit in the dev venv so the audit is locally reproducible.

findings.location: module docstring ('Rollout scope, honestly stated') vs implemented routing
findings.line: sandbox.py:19-29 vs bash.py:146-176, config.py:1178-1181 and 1243-1269, tools.py:1802-1809 (QA), 1846-1852 (devops)
findings.finding: The module docstring states the sandbox is wired into 'the three fully-generic, denylist-only bash tools' and that 'the other ~12 already-allowlist-scoped bash handlers (test-runner, dependency-audit, QA, devops, etc.) are intentionally NOT wired to this yet'. The code contradicts this: _run_bash_command_raw routes every caller through run_sandboxed when bash_sandbox_enabled is True (default), and the toolchain-needing variants pass a real toolchain image plus per-variant network overrides - directly observed in the QA (tools.py:1807-1808) and devops (1850-1851) handlers. The stale statement misled this audit's own initial scoping (an apparent 'QA reads host files' issue that is actually contained by the default sandbox).
findings.evidence: sandbox.py:19-29; bash.py:146-176 (routing + image/network pass-through); config.py:1178-1181 (default True), 1243-1269 (toolchain image + network=host overrides for test_runner/qa/refactor/migration); tools.py:1802-1809, 1846-1852.
findings.production_impact: Documentation-only: operators/future auditors may believe most bash variants run unsandboxed, mis-assess risk, or skip prerequisite setup (building gridiron-bash-toolchain:latest). Same doc-vs-code contradiction class as ORCH-04-106; cross-flagged to audit 11.
findings.recommendation: Update the docstring to the current rollout reality (denylist-only variants -> minimal image; toolchain variants -> toolchain image + documented network exceptions; host fallback only on explicit opt-out).
